title: Phone: OSP AMBER Desk Wants a Decision and a Time, 16:07

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Exhibit Hall B Command Post Speakerphone

caller.name: Trooper Ellen Hask
caller.label: OSP Northern Communications Center, AMBER Desk

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Lieutenant, Trooper Ellen Hask, OSP Northern Comms, AMBER desk. I've got you on speaker, so I'm assuming your Communications Supervisor and your sergeant are in the room. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Okay. Before I can take any request, I need your Communications Supervisor to tell me on this line that your LEDS/NCIC entry carries the Child Abduction flag, who did the second-person read-back, and the time it was logged. I won't take it from the screen alone. Go ahead when you're ready.

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Got it, I'm writing that down. Criterion four I already have. She's six. If you're requesting an alert, I need three more things from you right now.

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: First, one sentence on why you believe this is an abduction and that she's in danger. Not a lost child. Your food-booth sighting, has that been cleared? Tell me.

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Second, ONE vehicle description your sergeant will stand behind. Sergeant, that's on you. 'Dark blue or gray' is the most I'll carry. I'm not putting black Dodge, silver Chevy or anybody's name in the text. If you've got anything off that parking-lot photo, like body style or something in the bed, give it to me now.

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Third, the direction of travel and the time window. Which way out of the north gate, and between what times?

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: One more thing. Your WrenAlert people called me too, asking whether they can 'just send it.' They can't. WrenAlert doesn't carry AMBER. Please make sure they stand down on that.

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: If you go with a search-area WEA through your Emergency Management, or an Endangered Missing Person advisory, that's your call. Just tell me so I can close my file. So which is it, Lieutenant, and what time do I write down for your decision?

transcript.speaker: OSP AMBER Desk
transcript.text: Last thing. If you request, the plan has you notify the FBI Portland Field Office, NCMEC and Oregon Emergency Management, in that order. Who's making those calls, and what time do I log?

voiceStyles.OSP AMBER Desk: Man in his late 30s, calm and businesslike, speaking at a steady pace like someone filling in a form. Quiet communications center behind him, keyboard clicks, a radio murmur now and then. A little firmer on 'I won't take it from the screen alone' and 'ONE vehicle description.'

instructorNote: This is the main AMBER decision point. Pause at each prompted line. COMMS should confirm the Child Abduction-flagged entry and the 14:31 Console 2 read-back from the log. The IC, with the Undersheriff on the phone, marks all five criteria yes or no with a reason on the worksheet, picks an OSP AMBER request, a search-area WEA or an Endangered Missing Person advisory, and records the decision time. INV should commit to one description: older full-size pickup, dark blue or gray, light toolbox, no canopy, northbound from the north gate around 13:50. Watch that nobody uses WrenAlert and nobody names a suspect.
